properties.description:
Upon inspection of the sewer line three separate root intrusions were identified between the home and the city tap indicating multiple points of failure throughout the system. Given the overall condition of the line we recommend a full replacement of the sewer line from the home to the city connection approximately 40 feet in length to provide a long-term solution and prevent recurring issues.

Our scope of work includes full excavation from the home to the city tap removal of the existing damaged sewer line and installation of new piping for the entire run. This will eliminate all root intrusion points and restore proper flow throughout the system. All new piping will be properly bedded in sand to help prevent ground shifting and ensure long-term stability. Upon completion we will perform backfill and restore the work area.

properties.description:
Replacing cast iron pipes with pvc pipes and running a main building sewer line to the city.

Per contractor agent 
The project involves replacing an aging cast iron plumbing system located beneath the home by tunneling under the foundation. This method allows access to the existing sewer lines without the need to disturb or remove interior flooring. A tunnel will be carefully excavated beneath the structure to expose the old cast iron pipes which have likely deteriorated over time due to corrosion scaling and potential cracking.
Once exposed the outdated cast iron piping will be removed and replaced with new durable PVC piping. PVC (polyvinyl chloride) is resistant to corrosion has a longer lifespan and provides improved flow efficiency compared to cast iron. The new system will be installed to meet current plumbing codes and ensure reliable wastewater drainage.
In addition the property will be transitioned from an outdated backyard septic system to the municipal sewer system. This will involve connecting the new PVC plumbing to the city sewer line ensuring proper alignment grading and compliance with local regulations. The septic system will be properly abandoned according to code. This upgrade will provide a more efficient low-maintenance and environmentally compliant wastewater solution for the home. 
The job will take place in the front side of the house and underneath.

properties.description: We ran approximately 60 feet of 1-1/4 poly with riser to supply gas to an outdoor pool Heater. Prior to running gas we called Texas gas with a BTU count and was approved to tie in just after the meter. Tracer wire is laid in trench where the poly is laid. We painted all exposed Threaded pipe. An iron body valve is ahead of all the poly and riser and an additional 1/4 turn WOG valve is at the heater.  we will be testing the system with compress air at a tee just passed the iron body valve as to not turn off the gas supply to the house. We tried to get this inspected in December but were slowed due to existing and expired permits from other contractors now that all has been passed we are seeking an inspection and permission to turn on the supply to the pool heater and cover the entire trench.  The homeowner covered the trench but left the risers exposed. He was concerned as he had an employee Christmas party and didnt want anyone to trip on the excavation. I do have pictures and the depth of the poly is at 20 to the top of the pipe. Approximately 55 bags of all-purpose sand were used to bed (and cover) the poly before it was partially backfilled. Dig TESS was called before and excavation from a third party hired by the homeowner began excavation.  Thank you Kindley and my apologies if we had a missed inspection. Install new cleanouts as required by current code.
Ensure proper flow line elevations and venting per Austin Water and UPC/IPC requirements.

properties.description:
The project involves replacing the existing waste line that runs from the house to the citys sewer tie-in. This is a crucial task that requires the careful removal and replacement of the current waste line infrastructure to ensure proper drainage and waste management. Over time waste lines can degrade due to factors such as wear and tear tree root intrusion shifting ground or pipe corrosion leading to potential blockages or leaks. In this case the waste line needs to be fully replaced to ensure that the connection between the house and the citys main sewer system functions efficiently and complies with local plumbing codes and regulations.

The process of changing out the waste line begins with a thorough inspection of the existing system. This involves assessing the current pipe condition identifying any issues like cracks leaks or clogs and determining the best course of action for replacement. In some cases it may also be necessary to conduct soil tests to assess ground conditions before excavation work begins. Once the assessment is complete a team of licensed plumbers and excavation specialists will begin the process of digging up the old waste line carefully extracting it and laying down a new durable pipe that meets modern standards for waste management.

This new pipe will be securely connected to the houses plumbing system at one end and to the citys sewer system at the other ensuring an airtight and reliable connection. The installation will also include checks for proper slope and alignment as waste lines must maintain a specific gradient to allow for the efficient flow of wastewater. After the new pipe is installed the trench will be backfilled and the surrounding area restored to its original condition.In addition to improving the functionality of the plumbing system this project will help prevent potential health hazards water damage and environmental risks caused by leaks or blockages in the old waste line.

This involves assessing the current pipe condition identifying any issues like cracks leaks or clogs and determining the best course of action for replacement. In some cases it may also be necessary to conduct soil tests to assess ground conditions before excavation work begins. Once the assessment is complete a team of licensed plumbers and excavation specialists will begin the process of digging up the old waste line carefully extracting it and laying down a new durable pipe that meets modern standards for waste management.

This new pipe will be securely connected to the houses plumbing system at one end and to the citys sewer system at the other ensuring an airtight and reliable connection. The installation will also include checks for proper slope and alignment as waste lines must maintain a specific gradient to allow for the efficient flow of wastewater. After the new pipe is installed the trench will be backfilled and the surrounding area restored to its original condition.In addition to improving the functionality of the plumbing system this project will help prevent potential health hazards water damage and environmental risks caused by leaks or blockages in the old waste line.. Trench and install floor drain to middle bar. 	Trench and install floor drain to middle bar.
Work will consist doing a scan of the concrete flooring where the trench will be exposed for any post tension cables water lines rebar etc. and then we will proceed with exposing a trench through the concrete floor behind the middle bar area. We will also be using a plastic set up and an air scrubber to cover all areas that may be affected by dust or equipment during the excavation and backfill process. Once it is exposed we will be installing a PVC floor drain that will tie into the existing drain behind the bar that heads to the small grease trap. Once the PVC drain is completely installed it will tested for proper functioning and for any leaks and upon passing of inspection the trench will then be back filled and the concrete flooring will be re-patched.
Timeframe: Job will take roughly 3 days to finish from start of excavation.
